Alex — great questions. Short answers to unblock planning, Marissa will go into technical depth on the call.

1) Schema versioning: the attached schema-example.json is draft-07 compatible. For the POC we recommend using draft-07 validators — we’ll version the schema in the repo and tag any breaking changes.

2) Constrained decoding: Redwood supports a pair of approaches:
   - Token-level constraints (lexical constraints) via an allowlist/denylist on token sequences for critical fields.
   - Sampler controls (top-k/top-p) and deterministic beam fallback when strictness is required.
We usually combine both: constrained decoding for the most structured fields, sampler controls for descriptive fields.

3) Retry & idempotency: include an Idempotency-Key header (we recommend UUIDv4) on requests. Redwood will honor the header for a 60s window for automatic safe retries; beyond that, best-effort deduping is applied and we log potential duplicates. We’ll share an SDK snippet in the tech sync.

Next: Marissa — can you propose 2 time slots tomorrow/Friday for a 45m tech sync? Also please add the HubSpot link and any pre-read for Sophie.

Thanks — Marcus

Hi Alex / Sophie —

Thanks everyone — looping in the technical details here and a quick integration checklist so the POC can start the moment we have calendar alignment.

Pre-read & files: I’ve attached schema-example.json (draft-07), and included a link to our docs for constrained-decoding: https://docs.redwood.ai/structured-output. Also attached is a small script (redwood-sdk-setup-commands.txt) with the Node install + auth steps.

Integration checklist (node/express example):
- SDK setup: npm i @redwood/inference@latest; set process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY. See redwood-sdk-setup-commands.txt for quick commands.
- Auth: use the API key for server-to-server POC; header X-Redwood-Idempotency for UUID per request. For production we recommend Vault/KMS to rotate keys (we can share our KMS integration doc).
- Request routing: set region = "us-west" (config) to pin the POC to your preferred region. For failover we recommend a policy: primary us-west -> fallback us-east; Redwood Console can automate that but for POC we'll hardcode routing in the SDK config.

Structured output reliability pattern (recommended):
1) Constrained decoding:
   - Apply token-level constraints for enumerated fields (status, reason_code).
   - For nested objects, enforce a strict start/end token pattern where possible.
2) Post-generation validation:
   - Validate the returned string against the draft-07 schema (we recommend ajv in Node).
   - If validation fails, run a 1st retry with tightened constraints (deterministic beam search + beam size 3).
   - If still invalid, call the reranker/embedding fallback: generate multiple candidates, embed each, and use your semantic reranker to pick the top candidate that validates.
3) Retry behavior & quotas:
   - Idempotency: use X-Redwood-Idempotency header (UUIDv4). Redwood will dedupe within 60s.
   - Backoff: linear backoff 500ms -> 1000ms -> 2000ms for up to 3 attempts.
   - Metrics: emit validation.failure, generation.retry, reranker.invocations to your monitoring so we can tune thresholds.

Code sketch (high-level):
- generate() -> constrained request -> if schema valid return -> else retry with deterministic beam -> if still invalid, call generateCandidates() -> embed & rerank -> pick top valid candidate or surface a structured error.

POC deliverables (2 weeks):
- Integration guide + working Node example (we’ll provide repo).
- Schema validation + metrics dashboard (Redwood Console).
- Failure-mode report after week 1 with suggested thresholds for sampling vs deterministic defaults.
